items.title: Supreme Court delivers split verdict on Centre's demand to send Election Commissioner appointment case to larger bench
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday delivered a split verdict on the Union government's demand to refer the petitions challenging the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 to a larger bench. The 2023 Act is under challenge for replacing the Chief Justice of India (CJI) with a Cabinet Minister on the selection panel which appoints Election Commissioners. The Central government had requested the Court to refer the matter to a larger bench under Article 145(3) of the Constitution. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma had reserved its decision on the demand for reference on July 30. Justice Datta rejected the government's request for reference. He went on to deliver a prima facie opinion on the challenge to the 2023 Act. "We heard these petitions for over 5 days, speaking in one voice would have served the voice of institutional cohesion. Unfortunately, we are divided in our opinion. It is a foundational principle of the constitutional scheme that rulers are bound by law and not above it," Justice Datta ruled. Justice Sharma disagreed with the observations made by Justice Datta.

items.title: Bedbugs in railway station VIP sofas: Court issues contempt notice to Divisional Railway Manager
items.summary: A railway court at Aurangabad has issued a show cause notice to the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Nanded division over bedbug infested sofas in the VIP room at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar railway station. Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) SM Aher warned the senior official of contempt of court proceedings for failing to address the issue despite earlier directions. The matter arose in May 2026 when Justice Manjusha Deshpande of Bombay High Court and her husband noticed old, pest-infested sofas in the VIP room and reported the matter. Justice Manjusha Ajay Deshpande On May 20, Magistrate Aher directed the DRM to carry out pest control and replace the old sofas so that inconvenience is not caused to the judges. However, railway authorities failed to take action or respond for nearly four months. In the show cause notice of September 19, the Court noted that judges are now forced to wait in their vehicles instead of using the designated lounge. “As the sofas in VIP room are having bed bugs, this is very disgusting position to sit on those sofas by Hon'ble High Court Judges i.e. very very important persons and they are now sitting in their cars instead of sitting in VIP room,”
